entries.title: Shared/Core update: run-terminal-command
entries.summary: Shared/Core, SDK changes across 2 file(s) (+51/−25).

ai.title: SDK rewrites Windows nul redirects to dev null
ai.summary: The SDK terminal tool now rewrites cmd-style `> nul` and `2> nul` redirections to `/dev/null` before running under Git Bash on Windows, preventing commands from creating an undeletable literal file named `nul`. This new behavior is grounded in the `rewriteWindowsNulRedirects` helper exported from sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts, which the `runTerminalCommand` Windows branch invokes on `command` before spawning bash. The shared parameter spec in common/src/tools/params/tool/run-terminal-command.ts also tightens the `command` input description to warn against cmd.exe syntax like `> nul` and rewrites `gitCommitGuidePrompt` to mandate bash HEREDOC commit messages.
ai.evidence: sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts adds the exported function `rewriteWindowsNulRedirects(command: string)` that regex-replaces `/([<>]\s*)nul(?![\w.])/gi` with `$1/dev/null` and calls it on `command` in the Windows branch before spawning bash; common/src/tools/params/tool/run-terminal-command.ts rewrites the `command` Zod field description and the git commit guidance in `gitCommitGuidePrompt` to mandate bash HEREDOC syntax and POSIX commands.

changes.what: Exports `rewriteWindowsNulRedirects` and applies it to `command` on the Windows branch before spawning bash, plus new tests asserting the rewrite behavior.
Rewrites the `command` field description and `gitCommitGuidePrompt` commit guidance to mandate bash HEREDOC syntax and warn against Windows `> nul` redirection to avoid creating a literal `nul` file.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: analytics-events
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+4/−1).

ai.title: Add DESKTOPPROJECTREMOVED analytics event
ai.summary: Added DESKTOP_PROJECT_REMOVED ('desktop.project_removed') to AnalyticsEvent enum in common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts. Enables tracking of desktop project removal actions. Scope: Shared/Core constants.

eli5.text: When you remove a project from the desktop app, the program now records that action as a distinct analytics event, so the team can see how often and when projects get deleted. You won't see any new popup or menu item yourself; this simply adds the 'desktop.project_removed' tracking label to the shared list of things the app already monitors. The change is live today and applies to all desktop users, enabling the team to track project removals just like they already track project openings and thread creations.

facts: The label/dots/perk-note logic is shared with Freebuff Desktop and lives in common; this module re-exports it and adds the terminal-layout gating only the CLI needs.
Days in a streak "week", the milestone the progress dots fill toward.

A week's worth of progress dots toward the 7-day milestone, e.g. "●●○○○○○". Fills to "●●●●●●●" at 7, then gains a trailing "+" ("●●●●●●●+") for any streak beyond the week so long runs read as "earned and still going" rather than just maxed out.

Fill toward the 7-day milestone, then stay full, a 19-day streak should read as fully earned, not roll back over into a partial second week. Past the week, a trailing "+" marks that the streak has run beyond the row.
"day" stays singular, it's a compound modifier ("7 day streak"), not a count of days on its own.

entries.title: CLI update: README
entries.summary: New files: `common/src/constants/freebuff-data-use.ts`.

ai.title: Data-use policy constants drive README copy and model tracing
ai.summary: The Freebuff data-use policy is now machine-readable: `FREEBUFF_DATA_USE_GENERATED_MARKDOWN_BLOCK` and `FREEBUFF_PUBLIC_DATA_USE_COPY` in the new `common/src/constants/freebuff-data-use.ts` feed `renderFreebuffDataUseFaqMarkdown()`, which `README.md` and `freebuff/cli/release/README.md` now use in place of the old hand-written FAQ lines. Per-model tracing follows the same source of truth, since `FREEBUFF_TRACED_MODEL_IDS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` now filters `FreebuffModelOption` objects by their new `dataUse` field instead of the removed `FREEBUFF_DATA_COLLECTION_WARNING` text.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/constants/freebuff-data-use.ts` defines `FREEBUFF_AI_TRAINING_NOTICE` ('May use data for AI training'), `FREEBUFF_PUBLIC_DATA_USE_COPY`, and `renderFreebuffDataUseFaqMarkdown()` and `renderFreebuffDataUseFaqMdx()`. `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` removes `FREEBUFF_DATA_COLLECTION_WARNING`, imports `FREEBUFF_AI_TRAINING_NOTICE` and `FreebuffModelDataUse`, adds a `dataUse` field to each `FreebuffModelOption`, and switches `FREEBUFF_TRACED_MODEL_IDS` to filter on `model.dataUse === 'training'`. `README.md` and `freebuff/cli/release/README.md` replace their old FAQ lines with generated data-use copy matching `FREEBUFF_PUBLIC_DATA_USE_COPY`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer renders the rollout banner or accepts the new `FreebuffModelDataUse` classification at runtime.

changes.what: Added machine-readable data-use constants and renderers in `freebuff-data-use.ts`.
Updated the model-selector warning comment to reference the AI-training notice.
Removed `FREEBUFF_DATA_COLLECTION_WARNING` and switched model tracing to the `dataUse` field.
Replaced old FAQ lines with generated data-use copy.
Replaced old FAQ lines with generated data-use copy in the packaged release README.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: cloud-plan-ready
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+14/−0).

ai.title: Cloud plan ready tool schema gains a required integrations list
ai.summary: The `cloudPlanReadyParams` input schema in `common/src/tools/params/tool/cloud-plan-ready.ts` now accepts a `required_integrations` array, letting the agent pass back the Gravity service slugs and names that need API keys or environment variables before a Freebuff Cloud plan can be approved. The native tool call example input was updated to match, including a sample `required_integrations` entry for the Resend service. This gives the planning agent a structured way to report which credential-bearing third-party services the agreed stack depends on, so the user-facing 'Start building' button can surface that list.
ai.evidence: The diff to `common/src/tools/params/tool/cloud-plan-ready.ts` adds a `required_integrations` field to the `cloudPlanReadyParams` input schema, defined as a zod array of objects each with `slug` and `name` string fields, and includes a matching entry in the `input` object of the `$getNativeToolCallExampleString` call.
